targets.title: Discretionary tax changes and the macroeconomy: new narrative evidence from the united kingdom
targets.evidence_quote:
We first computationally reproduce all impulse response figures and regression
results in Cloyne (2013) using the data and code provided by the authors on the
AER website.
targets.outcome_computational_quote:
We first complete computational reproduction of all the main results of the paper,
and using author-provided data and code, were able to reproduce the coefficients
exactly.
targets.outcome_robustness_quote:
The shape of the output response to these narrative tax shocks appears fairly
robust to our tests. In general we find these results to be fairly robust.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Original code reproduces coefficients exactly. The authors judge the substantive response fairly robust overall; weaker results largely arise from short lag structures they consider inadequate or aggressive exclusion of rare shocks. Their explicit interpretation governs the robustness verdict.

reasoning: The report re-runs Cloyne’s own data and code, then changes specifications. Romer and Romer supply narrative-shock context and are not re-tested as an independent target. No target DOI is printed in the reference entry.
